# RustyNES v2.7.0 — "Palisade"

The first release of the audit line that [ADR 0041](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-hardware-release-is-v3.0.0.md) put between v2.6.23 and the SuperStation One core, which is now **v3.0.0**. It works from the core audit in [`docs/audits/`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/README.md), and its subject is one boundary: **a save-state file is untrusted input**, and until now a corrupt one could crash the emulator.

**AccuracyCoin 144/144** (RAM decoder) and **nestest** re-run on the release tree: both green. The full `--features test-roms` workspace suite, run with the one audio behaviour change below, passed **2,612 tests, 0 failed**, and moved no golden.

**The MiSTer sibling does not change in this release, and no new bitstream is cut.** No hardware has run any bitstream; the board session is v2.9.2.

## A corrupt save state fails at restore, not one tick later

Every crash this closes has the same shape, and it is the reason nothing caught them: the value **restores without complaint**, and the panic fires on the *next* tick as an out-of-bounds index into a fixed table. On a release build (`panic = "abort"`) that kills the process from a hand-edited `.rns`. Each bound is the hardware register's own width, so no state the emulator writes can trip one.

| Where | What is now rejected | Error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PPU | a sprite count above 8 (IMP-01) | `InvalidSprCount` |
| PPU | a raster position past dot 340 or the pre-render line | `InvalidRasterPosition` |
| PPU | fine X above 7, and ten sprite-evaluation and OAM-bus counters past the ranges the PPU keeps them in | `FieldOutOfRange`, naming the field |
| APU | twelve register-width fields: pulse duty and step, the three sweep fields, envelope volume/divider/decay, triangle step, DMC rate, bit count and DAC (IMP-02) | `FieldOutOfRange`, naming the field |
| Resampler | a zero sample rate; a non-finite or non-positive CPU rate; a phase outside `[0, 1)`; a non-finite filter or held value; a rate ratio above one host sample per CPU cycle | `InvalidResampler` |
| Bus | an OAM-DMA byte index above 255 while a transfer is active, or above 256 after | `SectionInvalid` |
| Container | a section length that overflows `usize` (IMP-03, real on 32-bit `wasm32`) | `SectionTruncated` |

The resampler row deserves a sentence: those values never panicked. They **hung** the emulation thread in `add_sample`'s `while phase >= 1.0` loop, or filled the audio with NaN — and a *finite* but huge rate ratio hangs exactly like an infinite one, which is why the ratio is bounded and not merely its finiteness.

Two smaller fixes ride along. `SectionIter` now stops after its first error; before, a malformed section could not advance its cursor, so every later call returned the same error forever — an infinite iterator for any caller that skips errors. And a restored `dma_mc_consumed` is discarded: it is structurally zero at any instruction boundary, release builds already drained and discarded it, and loading it only served to trip a dev-profile assertion.

## The fuzz target could not find any of this. Now it can

`fuzz/fuzz_targets/save_state.rs` has existed since v2.2.0. It **restored and stopped** — so every deferred panic above was invisible to it — and it fed raw bytes with no corpus, so almost no input got past the header and section framing to reach a field at all.

It now works differently, for three measured reasons:

- **Patch mode.** An even first byte makes the rest of the input a list of `(offset, value)` patches over a *real* snapshot. Structure survives, and every field is one patch away.
- **It runs the machine after an accepted restore** — about three scanlines, not a whole frame. A frame per case measured **~15 executions per second**; this runs at **~1,000**.
- **The base machine exercises the paths.** A silent APU hides the channel panics, because a pulse channel with a zero length counter returns before it ever indexes its duty table; rendering has to be on for sprite evaluation to run. The synthetic ROM now starts all four tone channels and turns rendering on.

Run against the **unfixed** tree, with each defect it found fixed in turn so the next could surface, it found five crashes: a restored `dma_mc_consumed` tripping an invariant (6,848 runs), IMP-01 at `ppu.rs:5104` (29,326), the OAM-DMA index overflow (287,867), the raster position (76,381), and fine X (92,496). **Four of the five were not in the audit.** An audit finds what its reader thought to look for; a fuzzer that can reach the code finds what nobody did.

The fifth changed the method. One PPU field at a time, per fuzz round, is a slow way to find a class, so after fine X every field the PPU restore loads was read against the code that uses it, and ten more counters that are incremented without a mask were bounded to the ranges the running PPU keeps them in.

## Pulse 1 no longer mutes when its sweep is switched off

Writing `$08` to `$4001` — negate on, shift 0 — is the documented way to **disable** the sweep, and a common one. With it, pulse 1 computed its target as `c - c - 1` in wrapping 16-bit arithmetic, got `$FFFF`, read that as "target above `$7FF`", and **muted the channel**. NESdev's "APU Sweep" is explicit that a negative target clamps to zero and that negate mode never mutes. Pinned red on v2.6.23 by `pulse1_negate_shift0_clamps_to_zero_and_does_not_mute`; a companion test walks every shift from 1 to 7 over every period from 8 to `$7FF` and shows the clamp changes nothing else.

This was not in any audit. It surfaced while checking the RTL audit's claim that the *FPGA* core mutes here — the RTL was right and the oracle was wrong. Because the sibling already followed the wiki, the co-simulation ladder compared two models that disagreed only in a place no stimulus visited. v2.8.2 adds the gate.

## Also

- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` on `rustynes-cpu`, `-ppu`, `-apu`, `-mappers` and `-core`. None contained `unsafe`; this makes that a compile-time guarantee, and it holds on the `thumbv7em` `no_std` build.
- Every new check was mutated out and its test re-run: **39 mutations, 39 caught.**
- `docs/apu-2a03.md`'s sweep-mute entry was itself wrong ("the negated target underflows below 8") and is corrected.

## What is not claimed

- The `SectionIter` overflow can happen only where `usize` is 32 bits. The `thumbv7em` build compiles the fix; no test executes it on a 32-bit target.
- No hardware has run any bitstream.

Full detail: [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) and the [core ledger](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/core-disposition.md).
